svg.title: myOS Native Scheduler and SMP Architecture
svg.desc: Current native scheduler: Windows, Linux, Android integration work and native driver hosts share per-CPU round-robin scheduling, bounded wakeup boost, work stealing and deadlines. Date-scoped performance evidence at bottom.
svg.text: One scheduler for every execution environment • per-CPU scheduling, wait/wake, deadlines and lifecycle
Architecture verified against master · 9 October 2026 · historical performance below is from 1 October 2026
Execution environments — all threads ultimately use the native scheduler
• Native thread execution via Linux ABI
Native myOS kernel — SMP scheduling authority (ring 0)
Scheduling mechanisms are shared; each environment supplies only its own ABI semantics.
• A separate queue on each online CPU
• Signal / alert meaning stays in ABI
• Safe handling when wait setup fails
• Thread never runs on two CPUs
Per-CPU scheduling state — no system-wide runqueue lock on the common dispatch path
Local Ready queue • FIFO ready list
Own timer and deadlines • Own runqueue lock
Local Ready queue • FIFO ready list
Own timer and deadlines • Own runqueue lock
Local Ready queue • FIFO ready list
Own timer and deadlines • Own runqueue lock
Local Ready queue • FIFO ready list
Own timer and deadlines • Own runqueue lock
Migration: idle stealing and periodic rebalancing; active stack ownership is protected
Supporting native mechanisms — not separate personality schedulers
Measured k3s idle baseline — Proxmox, 2 vCPU, 60-second window, 1 October 2026
Evidence scope: these measurements are NOT wake-to-run latency, nor a comparison with Linux/Windows; CPU hotplug and NUMA placement remain unproven.
